title: erpax — a zero-entropy, content-addressed ERP corpus
description:
erpax is an ERP corpus in which every folder under src/ is one irreducible atom told three ways (form · code · proof), wired through a single content-uuid. Its law is zero entropy ⇒ infinite tamper-cost: a claim is enforced by a gate that blocks its violation, never by prose that asks for compliance.

Machine-checked proof, as of v1.0.6 (2026-09-18). The decisions that carry consequences are defined in Lean 4 and proved there, with the TypeScript as a checked twin: src/verify/lean/Release.lean ↔ the release decision, Arrival.lean ↔ the landing verdict, Uuid.lean ↔ the v8 uuid layout. Each twin’s test reads its .lean file for every theorem name it relies on, so a theorem cannot quietly disappear.

The inventory, kernel-checked with Lean 4.33.1 and counted rather than asserted: 105 theorems across 12 files, every one accepted by the kernel and none resting on sorry. 65 depend on no axioms at all (closed by decide over a stated finite domain); 40 rest on Lean’s own propext and Quot.sound, reached through core list and arithmetic lemmas. None uses native_decide, which would trust the compiler instead of the kernel.

What is proved, and what is not. Earlier releases carried 15 declarations in three files that did not compile and 4 sorry stubs; those files claimed properties of ARBITRARY data (that any list of loop states rises, that any ledger is append-only) and several were false as written or dischargeable by fabricating a witness. They are now stated about the OPERATIONS that produce the data — a gated publish, a folded refinement step, a computed convergence — so each guarantee holds by construction. A theorem proves its DECISION, never the facts it is fed: no proof here makes a red build green, a forged digest verify, or a divergent computation convergent, and none of it claims a Millennium problem is solved.
